contradicting_evidence: A near-term upward interpretation has some support: BTC and ETH hourly taker-buy shares were approximately 54.6% and 64.7%, and ETH/BTC also advanced during that hour.
A near-term downward interpretation has substantial competing support: only 16 of 100 breadth constituents advanced over 24h, while BTC and ETH remained down approximately 1.29% and 2.79%.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A relief extension and a fade back into weakness are both credible. The latest positive hour supports stabilization attempts, but not enough evidence exists to favor a higher or lower endpoint over the next 12h. BTC resilience should not be read as broad altcoin recovery.
falsification_conditions: Repeated positive closes with sustained spot buying, stronger ETH/BTC and widening participation would replace the no-edge assessment with an upward case.
Failure of the rebound followed by persistent negative closes, renewed selling pressure and continued weak participation would establish a downward case.
missing_evidence: Subsequent completed hourly candles showing whether the rebound holds or fails.
Repeated order-book and trade-flow observations; the supplied microstructure snapshots cannot establish persistence.
A derivatives sequence distinguishing sustained demand from position reduction; hourly funding-event rates are unavailable.
supporting_evidence: The completed hour showed BTC up 0.33%, ETH up 0.65% and ETH/BTC up 0.31%, opposing a simple immediate-downside extrapolation.
BTC and ETH prices rose while open interest fell approximately 0.52% and 0.89%. This is consistent with position reduction or short covering, not confirmation of fresh risk-taking.
The rebound sits against negative 24h breadth and altcoin underperformance, leaving opposing signals across observation windows.
Near-zero or negative live funding does not show positive-funding exuberance, but also does not establish an upward catalyst.
